# Accessibility

Breader is for everyone who reads. If something stops you reading or listening, that's a bug, and it comes first.

## What's there now

- **Type you can change.** Five typefaces, among them Atkinson Hyperlegible, made for low vision. Text size from 15 to 32, three weights, line spacing and line length.
- **Five themes.** Auto, Day, Warm, Dusk and Night. Auto follows your device's light or dark setting.
- **Read aloud.** Any book can be read to you, each sentence marked as it's spoken, with the screen locked too.
- **Less motion.** If your device asks for reduced motion, Breader's animations follow it.
- **Keys while listening.** Space or K to play and pause, J and L to go back and on, and the arrows, as a video player has.
- **Labels for screen readers** on buttons that show only an icon.

## Where it works

Breader runs in a web browser on phones and computers, and can be added to your home screen to open like an app. It's built for current browsers; older ones may miss parts.

## What's not good enough yet

- PDFs are shown as their pages, so their text can't be resized or restyled.
- Not yet tested end to end with VoiceOver, TalkBack or NVDA.
- Not every part has full keyboard shortcuts yet.
- Read aloud was tuned on computers first and may be rougher on phones.

## Telling us about a barrier

Open a [bug report](https://github.com/anubhav-qt/breader/issues/new?template=bug.yml) and add the `accessibility` label, or ask in [Discussions](https://github.com/anubhav-qt/breader/discussions/categories/q-a). Say what you use (screen reader, zoom, switch, keyboard) and where you got stuck.
